---
title: "![](/assets/node-icons/PassDown.svg){height=20} PassDown"
---

The PassDown node can be thought of as a Basin without storage. It fully 'passes-down' flow, so the sum of the inflow is always equal to the sum of the outflow. As such, the PassDown node does not need any profile information. The general concept is:

- The PassDown node receives flow from other nodes which provide flow: connector nodes, FlowBoundary or other PassDown nodes
- The PassDown node directs this flow to flow receiving nodes: Basins, level boundaries, terminals, user demands or other PassDown nodes

PassDown nodes can be chained arbitrarily, as long as there are no loops. Multiple PassDown nodes can flow into the same PassDown node (a confluence), in which case the inflows are summed. Over such chains, which are subgraphs of the model consisting of PassDown and potentially UserDemand nodes, flow travels instantaneously. PassDown nodes can also distribute flows over multiple nodes downstream, using the flow fraction of the links.

Flow cannot be split directly by nodes that are not PassDown nodes: a connector node (e.g. Pump or Outlet), FlowBoundary or UserDemand has a single outflow link. To divide such flow, put a PassDown node in between.

# Tables

## Static

The fractions are defined per link from the PassDown node `node_id` to the node `to_node_id`. All outflow links have a fraction, except the link to a UserDemand node, which gets the abstraction instead. This table is optional for PassDown nodes that do not divide their flow: a single outflow link gets the whole flow.

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
%run ../../gen_docs_table.py
table_from_schema("PassDown.Static", restrictions = {"to_node_id": "Must be a node downstream of `node_id` that is not a UserDemand node", "fraction": "Must be in [0,1]. The fractions of the outflow links of a node must sum to 1, where at most one may be unspecified and gets the remainder."})
```

# Equations

The algorithm for the PassDown node flow in a subgraph is as follows:

- Traverse the PassDown subgraph node-wise in topological order, so that every node comes after all nodes it depends on: the nodes upstream of it, and the UserDemand nodes that take precedence over it. UserDemands take precedence over PassDown nodes because the UserDemand abstracts before the remainder is passed down. Since the order is only well defined if there are no loops, loops in a PassDown subgraph are not allowed.
- For PassDown nodes:
    - Compute the total inflow
    $$
        q_\text{total in} = \sum q_\text{in}
    $$
    - Compute the corrected outflow
    $$
        q_\text{out} = q_\text{total in} - q_\text{ud},
    $$
    where $q_\text{ud}$ is the UserDemand abstraction given the effective total demand $d$:
    $$
        q_\text{ud} = \min(q_\text{total in}, d).
    $$
    Then the flow over each outflow link $l$, except the link to the UserDemand node, follows from the fraction $f_l$ of that link:
    $$
        q_l = f_l \cdot q_\text{out}.
    $$
- For UserDemand nodes it works like the standard [UserDemand flow](/reference/node/user-demand.qmd#equations), but without the low storage factor or minimum level.

Without allocation, a UserDemand abstracting from a PassDown node takes its demand before anything is passed on, regardless of its `demand_priority`: in a chain of PassDown nodes the upstream UserDemand is served first. Demand priorities are only applied by [allocation](#allocation), which bounds the abstraction of each UserDemand by what it allocated.

A model does not need a Basin when all flow comes from FlowBoundary nodes and passes through PassDown nodes, for instance into UserDemand or Terminal nodes. Allocation does require a Basin in each subnetwork.

## Tracers

With `experimental.concentration` the tracers are propagated through the PassDown subgraphs in the same order as the flow is computed, using the mass over the timestep rather than concentrations, so that no mass is lost when a flow is zero:

- For flows into a PassDown subgraph the mass is the flow times the concentration of the source: the concentration of the FlowBoundary or LevelBoundary, or of the Basin upstream of a Pump, Outlet or TabulatedRatingCurve. For a UserDemand outside the subgraph it is the mass in its return flow.
- The mass of the inflows of a PassDown node is mixed: the concentration of the flow out of a PassDown node, including the flow abstracted by a UserDemand, is the total mass in divided by the total volume out.
- A UserDemand abstracting from a PassDown node handles tracers like a UserDemand abstracting from Basins: the mass of the flow it abstracts ends up in its return flow, with the UserDemand tracer replaced by the one of the UserDemand itself.
- The mass that flows from a PassDown subgraph into a Basin is added to the mass of that Basin. A PassDown node itself does not store water, so tracers do not age in it.

## Allocation

PassDown nodes can be used in [allocation](/concept/allocation.qmd#sec-allocation-pass-down) subnetworks, where the UserDemand abstracting from a PassDown node abstracts up to its allocated demand and the rest of the flow is divided over the downstream nodes. A PassDown node must have the same subnetwork ID as the nodes it is connected to: PassDown nodes at the boundary between the primary network and a subnetwork, or between subnetworks, are not supported yet.

## Water quality

In the offline [Delwaq coupling](/guide/delwaq.qmd) a PassDown node has no volume, so it is removed from the Delwaq network like the connector nodes: each node that flows into the PassDown node gets an exchange with each node it flows into. The flow over such an exchange is the flow of the link into the PassDown node times the share of the outflow link in the total outflow, per timestep, so the mixing in the PassDown node is the same as in the [tracers](#tracers) of the core. An exchange between two boundary nodes, like a FlowBoundary and the UserDemand that abstracts from the PassDown node, is dropped, since it does not touch a Basin.

# Junction or PassDown {#junction-or-passdown}

Both nodes have no storage, but they play different roles:

| | Junction | PassDown |
|---|---|---|
| Role | Draws the network, it is removed before the simulation | A node in the simulation, with a flow state per outflow link |
| Downstream level seen by a weir or pump upstream | The level of the Basin or LevelBoundary behind the Junction | None: the structure always has free outflow |
| Splitting flow | Not possible, the flow over each link follows from the nodes it connects | By the fractions of the outflow links |
| UserDemand abstraction | No | At most one UserDemand per PassDown node |
| Bidirectional flow | Yes | No, the inflow comes from Pump, Outlet, TabulatedRatingCurve, FlowBoundary, UserDemand or PassDown nodes |
| Results | No flows of its own | Flows per link in the flow results |

Use a Junction to draw a confluence or bifurcation whose flows are determined by the connected nodes, for instance between a Basin and several resistances. Use a PassDown node where the flow is imposed by the structures upstream and must be divided, abstracted from or passed on without a Basin in between.

# Connectivity rules

The PassDown node has some specific connectivity rules:

- A maximum of 1 UserDemand node can abstract from a PassDown node.
- A node that is not a PassDown node (a connector node, FlowBoundary or UserDemand) has a single outflow link. To divide its flow, use a PassDown node in between.
- Multiple nodes can flow into the same PassDown node, but the PassDown nodes and the UserDemand nodes that abstract from them cannot form a loop.
- A UserDemand node must have either one or more Basin inflow links, or exactly one PassDown inflow link.
- Since a PassDown node cannot accumulate water, it always needs one or more outflow links. If the PassDown node flows into a UserDemand node, there must be another outflow link, because the inflow to the PassDown can be larger than the demand and the remainder needs somewhere to go.
